newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac says NATO-Russia pact ends Yalta divisions.
newsitem.headline: Chirac says NATO-Russia pact ends Yalta divisions.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said on Tuesday a partnership agreement between NATO and Russia would abolish forever the division of Europe that resulted from the Yalta summit at the end of World War Two.

"The order that came out of Yalta led to a peace that was unfair, preserved by the balance of terror," Chirac said at a summit to sign a NATO-Russia "Founding Act". "The Paris accord does not shift the divisions created in Yalta. It does away with them once and for all."
Chirac said the agreement enshrining NATO-Russia cooperation on European security would sweep away the last vestiges of the East-West Cold War, eight years after the fall of the Berlin Wall.

France, which was not invited to the 1945 summit in the Crimea between U.S. president Franklin Roosevelt, Soviet leader Josef Stalin and British prime minister Winston Churchill, had always opposed the division of Europe, he said.
"Today, we are building peace. We are turning the page on half a century of incomprehension, confrontation and division on our continent," he said.
U.S. President Bill Clinton, Russian President Boris Yeltsin and NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana were among the leaders who attended the glittering ceremony at the Elysee presidential palace.
